issue: #374 — apply --canary-machine performed a real apply (the whole fleet, with a --yes nobody typed) and --refresh-only rewrote every lock without ever reaching check_operator_auth; a read mode carrying --pre-script ran the script before the refusal

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim
refuted_claims: Gate every apply mode including the reads — REFUTED: check_operator_auth iterates every machine regardless of --machine, so a listed operator would lose `apply -m theirs --check` for zero confidentiality gain; the reads stay open and the line is pinned in both directions.

Fixing the gate position also fixes the unconfirmed rollout — REFUTED: independent defects; the gate tests pass --yes explicitly so the restored prompt cannot mask an unreached gate, and the prompt test runs as the authorized operator so the gate cannot mask the missing prompt.

The hook exemption misses --post-script (agy charge) — COUNTERED: post_script runs at one site inside apply_execute (dispatch_apply_b.rs:465), unreachable from any read mode; adding it would only over-refuse.

Exempting --check is a confidentiality leak (agy charge) — DIVERGENCE recorded, not accepted: apply --check prints what the ungated check/plan/graph verbs print to anyone; gating one spelling of the read buys nothing.
quorum.divergence: the agy lane refuted four of five charges against the first tree; three were accepted and fixed in the same branch (abort-on-drift is not a read; the gate honours --machine; the fleet leg asks once), each pinned by a falsifier measured RED without its hunk; the post-script charge was countered by the call site and the --check charge is recorded as a design divergence

systems: Terraform Cloud/Enterprise — run tasks and Sentinel evaluate who may apply before any apply; a targeted or partial apply is still an apply
Ansible Tower/AWX — execute permission and credentials are bound per job template; --limit narrows hosts, never the permission check
Pulumi — stack permissions gate `up`; `--target` is still `up`
Salt — publisher_acl gates who may publish which functions to which minions; a batch of one is still a publish
crux.verdict: at the industry default after this branch: the operator check is positional and runs before any exit, hook or backup; no invocation shape (canary, refresh, pre-hook) routes around it, and the reads that every ungated verb already serves stay open

agy_teamwork.verdict: five charges: three accepted and fixed (abort-on-drift read bypass; scoped-operator regression from the every-machine iteration; N prompts on the fleet leg), one countered (post-script is unreachable from a read), one recorded as divergence (--check exemption); its 'below the industry default' verdict described the tree before the three fixes
unique_findings: --canary-machine calls cmd_apply directly and skips apply_pre_checks, so --pre-script/--webhook-before/--abort-on-drift are silently ignored on the canary path — pre-existing, filed as its own ticket
--backup is a silent no-op in read modes — known limit; a read takes no backup because it changes nothing

pmat.quality_gate: zero vacuous tests in the falsifier or any file this branch touches; clippy --all-targets -D warnings 0; fmt clean

falsification.test: eleven cases run the built binary against a two-machine fixture with allowed_operators: [alice]: the ordinary apply refuses mallory (control); --canary-machine refuses mallory, writes nothing, converges no other machine; --refresh-only refuses; --pre-script does not run for mallory, in an apply or in a --check; alice keeps --check with a hook and keeps the canary rollout; a --check flag does not launder a canary rollout; and as alice with no --yes the fleet leg does not converge; plus the three round-2 cases: --check --abort-on-drift is refused for mallory; bob listed on sandbox alone keeps apply -m sandbox and is refused -m prod and unscoped; three machines with two y answers converge both remaining machines with exactly one fleet prompt
falsification.reverted: src/cli/dispatch_apply_b.rs and src/cli/apply_variants.rs -> the merge-base's (9e0815c0), tests kept
falsification.observed_failure: src/cli/dispatch_apply_b.rs, apply_variants.rs, dispatch_apply.rs, apply_from_plan.rs at the merge-base, tests kept: first binary 8 of 14 RED — canary_apply_refuses_an_unlisted_operator, canary_apply_writes_nothing_when_refused, canary_apply_does_not_converge_the_rest_of_the_fleet, canary_apply_does_not_imply_yes, refresh_only_refuses_an_unlisted_operator, an_unauthorized_apply_does_not_run_the_pre_script, a_read_mode_does_not_launder_the_pre_script_hook, a_read_flag_does_not_launder_a_canary_rollout; second binary (round-2 hunks reverted, measured separately): 3 of 3 RED — a_check_with_abort_on_drift_is_not_a_read, a_machine_scoped_operator_keeps_their_own_machine, the_fleet_leg_asks_once_not_once_per_machine
falsification.still_green_when_reverted: the regression guards, by design: control_the_ordinary_apply_refuses_an_unlisted_operator, a_listed_operator_still_gets_a_read_with_a_hook, a_listed_operator_still_gets_a_canary_rollout, the_read_only_apply_modes_stay_ungated, an_unrestricted_config_is_unaffected, a_machine_scoped_operator_can_still_read_its_own_machine

evidence.redaction: no machine-local identity in this set
known_limits: check_operator_auth checks the machines the invocation names; the plan-file path carries no machine filter and keeps the full iteration.
--canary-machine still bypasses apply_pre_checks (pre-existing; its own ticket).
--backup with a read mode takes no backup and says nothing; a read changes nothing to back up.
The redundant per-exit copy #370 added on the --plan-file path is left in place.
